decision_reason: A1 already separates jogging and stairs through several locomotor properties, although stairs has the weakest seen coverage. The more actionable gaps are among low-translation manual activities: writing differs from eating soup only in intensity, eating soup differs from eating sandwich only in smoothness, and drinking from cup is relatively close to folding clothes. Add wrist_orientation_excursion to describe local angular range independently of global posture and rotational-motion prominence. Retain the other concepts because further distinctions, including a new sitting-versus-standing cue, would require stronger assumptions about phone placement or habitual execution than the supplied information supports. The diagnostics guide semantic refinement, not claims of recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_orientation_excursion
attributes.definition: Angular range traversed by the watch-bearing wrist relative to gravity during an activity window, excluding rotation that leaves gravity-relative orientation unchanged. This describes local orientation range, not rotational speed, repetition rate, or global body posture.

levels.Low: Wrist orientation remains within a narrow gravity-relative range.
levels.Medium: Wrist orientation traverses a moderate gravity-relative range.
levels.High: Wrist orientation traverses a broad gravity-relative range.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable acceleration and rotation magnitude. Retains a transferable distinction between vigorous locomotion and quieter manual activities, with walking and dribbling providing seen intensity anchors for jogging. Wrist-dominant effort and phone carriage can make overall intensity ambiguous.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in recurring acceleration or rotation. Preserves jogging-versus-stairs information and transfers from seen gait and rapid manual repetition. Irregular actions, brief windows, and multiple plausible repeating units can obscure cadence.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid signal change. Preserves continuous-versus-fluctuating motion distinctions, including the existing soup-versus-sandwich contrast, without inventing food-specific cues. Small writing strokes, watch attachment, and motion speed can alter apparent smoothness.

impulsiveness: G10 supports isolated abrupt changes and impacts, distinct from sustained roughness. Retains a seen-supported impact contrast relevant to jogging versus stairs. Contact transmission and vigorous hand gestures can produce ambiguous peaks, so impacts do not identify gait by themselves.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation when the carried phone tracks body configuration. Preserves the existing sitting-versus-standing semantic distinction and inclination information for stairs. Its predictability is placement-dependent: an unconstrained phone or wrist orientation cannot reliably establish global posture, so no additional sitting-specific cue is asserted.

posture_variability: G12 supports gravity-relative configuration changes when phone movement reflects the body. Retains global stability-versus-reconfiguration information useful for folding clothes and locomotion. Loose carriage and isolated arm motion can confound interpretation; this attribute must not be inferred solely from wrist reorientation.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular-motion prominence in gyroscope signals. Preserves a transferable distinction between rotational manual actions and quieter hand use. Rapid small rotations and slower broad rotations can have similar prominence, motivating a separate orientation-range concept rather than changing this definition.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies. Retains walking as a meaningful seen anchor for jogging and stairs despite stairs' weak A1 coverage. Inertial proxies do not establish sustained travel or stair height directly, and arm excursions can resemble translation; no vertical-progression attribute is added.

motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal consistency independently of repetition speed. Preserves the existing drinking-from-cup versus folding-clothes distinction and transfers from structured versus irregular seen manual actions. Pauses, execution style, and window boundaries can weaken this class-level expectation.

wrist_orientation_excursion: G12, with G1 and G2 as complementary evidence, supports the range of changing gravity-relative watch orientation. Constrained writing can involve a narrower orientation range than hand-to-mouth transport or garment manipulation, adding a plausible contrast to the one-coordinate writing-versus-soup pair. Cup tilting may also distinguish drinking from spoon transport without assuming food recognition. Seen typing, eating soup, and eating pasta provide constrained-to-reorienting manual anchors. Expected predictability is limited by watch-side participation, wrist-versus-elbow strategy, windows containing only a hold, and dynamic acceleration; cup drinking and folding may overlap, so this is not asserted as a guaranteed separator.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes distinguish magnitude, repetition rate, sustained roughness, isolated peaks, global mean inclination, global posture change, rotational prominence, locomotor progression, temporal predictability, and local wrist orientation range. Wrist orientation excursion is not a renamed posture-variability attribute: its scope is explicitly the watch-bearing wrist rather than the load-bearing body. It also differs from rotational prominence because repeated small rotations can be prominent while remaining within a narrow orientation range. Correlation among intensity, cadence, roughness, and impacts is possible but does not make their physical meanings identical. No class separation is guaranteed, particularly for sitting versus standing under unconstrained phone carriage or for overlapping eating and drinking strategies.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
